title: Caching strategies (client and server)
summary: Cache to cut latency and load, at the cost of staleness. On mobile, layer memory, disk and HTTP caches, and decide per data type how stale is acceptable.
requirements: Know the access pattern (read-heavy? hot keys?) and the acceptable staleness per data type.
Bound memory and disk usage; survive app restarts where useful.
components: Memory cache (NSCache / LRU) for decoded objects and images
Disk cache (files or SQLite) for responses and media, with size and age limits
HTTP cache (URLCache + ETag / Cache-Control) for server-controlled freshness
Server side: CDN for static media, Redis/Memcached in front of databases
tradeoffs: Cache-aside is simple and resilient but can serve stale data until TTL or invalidation.
Write-through keeps cache consistent but adds write latency; write-back is fast but risks data loss.
Stale-while-revalidate gives instant UI with eventual freshness; needs UI that tolerates updates in place.
Longer TTLs mean fewer requests and more staleness; push-based invalidation is fresher but more complex.
body: **Invalidation** is the hard part: TTLs, explicit invalidation on write (e.g. after the user edits their profile, update local cache optimistically), versioned keys, and server push (silent push or socket event) for shared data.
**Mobile specifics:** cache by user (clear on logout), respect Low Data Mode, purgeable `Caches/` directory can be cleared by the OS, encrypt sensitive cached data with Data Protection.
**Thundering herd:** coalesce concurrent misses for the same key (single-flight), add jitter to TTLs.
**Follow-ups:** What is the cache key for a paginated feed? How do you measure hit rate on device? How do you avoid showing another user's data after an account switch?

code.caption: Read path (stale-while-revalidate)
code.text:
UI requests feed
  -> memory cache hit?  show immediately
  -> else disk cache hit? show, mark stale
  -> fetch network (If-None-Match: etag)
       304 -> refresh timestamps
       200 -> write disk + memory, diff into UI
